findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. A reader can answer "what is this and why does it matter" before scrolling.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: The header explains why a page on Athena's site is mostly about another project, firstmate. Without this the page would be confusing; with it, the reader knows the page is a sample of Athena's output.
findings.source: "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project, taken at one fixed commit... This page is that study of firstmate."

findings.text: Next steps are linked from the top and are concrete: prerequisites, the clone command, `./setup.sh`, and an example `athena ask "add a changelog"`. The newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself." and the Next steps section

findings.text: The header promises that every result can be traced to the models used, the cost and the verdict, but this study never says which models wrote or checked it or what it cost. Athena's main selling point goes undemonstrated on its own front page.
findings.source: "get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict"

findings.text: Below the Start here section the page becomes a dense state machine of firstmate internals: 12 transition cards, exit codes and 45 claims. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has little reason to read it, and this is most of the page.
findings.source: Transitions section, e.g. t4 Guard: "worktree clean and committed work landed, whether the captain approved the merge, firstmate merged it under yolo, or a local-only ship landed by a guarded fast-forward..."

findings.text: This link sits in the header, but it is meant for the project owner. A first-time visitor is not that owner and is told nothing about what the proposals are.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: This section, and the finding f3 note that "A first reading of the pinned tree missed these paths", describe how the page was produced rather than anything a newcomer needs. They make the page look like internal output, not something written for visitors.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The Start here section reads well for someone who wants firstmate's workflow. It defines terms before using them and walks one task through its steps, so a curious reader can follow it.
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit."
